metadata.title: [Kernel] Preserve FP32 channel-FP8 verification logits
metadata.body:
## Purpose

Preserve FP32 verifier logits for the supported SM70 channel-FP8 head without changing checkpoint weights or scales. The DFlash2 proposal head retains its original FP16 output. Compact target top-k retains source value/ID bits and the existing cutoff/nucleus fallback.

This extends the existing head route rather than introducing a second quantization backend. AI assistance was used.

## Test Plan

Ordinary complete wheel, CUDA 12.8/Torch 2.10, four V100-SXM2-16GB GPUs at 300 W, TP4, original unsloth NVFP4 model and DFlash2 draft7, 256K maximum length, .92 memory utilization. Same-service 1K/8K, eight 600-token prompts at fixed seed, temperature .7/top-p .9/top-k 20, thinking disabled; warmed C4 and natural EOS. Teacher-forcing tests cover the changed head on fixed real prompt prefixes against original FP8 codes/BF16 scales with FP64 dense accumulation.

## Test Result

Final installed artifact passes native dependency checks and 18 GPU/fake/graph tests. Its 16 native libraries are byte-identical to the complete source build; Python source equality and regenerated wheel RECORD are verified. No private runtime extension or preload is required.

| Measurement | Main control | Candidate |
|---|---:|---:|
| 1K round latency | 14.137 ms | 14.143 ms |
| 8K round latency | 14.537 ms | 14.534 ms |
| 1K tokens/round, 95% CI | 3.034 [2.836, 3.227] | 3.056 [2.852, 3.247] |
| 8K tokens/round, 95% CI | 2.946 [2.875, 3.024] | 2.967 [2.884, 3.059] |
| C4 throughput | 438.15 token/s | 435.65 token/s |
| Reference-path fraction, 1K | 1.626% | 1.322% |
| Reference-path fraction, 8K | 2.080% | 1.478% |
| Draft graph kernels | 142 | 142 |

Acceptance intervals overlap, and three natural prompts end normally. Across 1040 teacher-forcing positions, head-only mean/p99/max KL is 1.053e-8 / 9.163e-8 / 9.923e-7, top-1 agreement is 100%, and recorded maximum logit error is .00408. This is head validation, not an FP64 oracle for the whole model.

There is no material round-latency improvement, and measured C4 throughput is .57% lower. Keep this PR in Draft: it does not pass the performance/concurrency gate. The initial shared FP32 proposal-output attempt added five draft graph kernels and regressed C4; preserving the original proposal output removes that regression but does not establish a speedup. A diagnostic oracle with an extra resident head shard ran out of memory at 8K; the final chunked oracle completes both lengths.
